notes: v503 — 🎯 Trade Plan, on every share's 📊 detail. Tonight's study proved that none of the twelve reports reliably predicts which way a share goes, so building a thirteenth would have been dishonest. Instead I asked the data what CAN be predicted, and got an emphatic answer: sort shares by how far they moved over the last 20 days and the ranking holds over the next 20 with a correlation of 0.89 on the ASX and 0.85 on the NYSE — the quietest tenth moving 0.31% a day and the wildest 5.73%. You cannot tell which way a share will go; you can tell how far it will move, almost exactly. The Trade Plan uses only that. It tells you how far the share moves, how many shares to buy so that a typical bad day costs the amount YOU choose to risk, where a stop can actually go (and warns you when the price steps are too coarse to give you the stop you think you have), how long it would take to sell out, its worst stretch in the stored year, and what the evidence honestly says. Nothing on it predicts direction. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5).
